security_audit.summary: Confirmed risks center on intentional Nmap reconnaissance, privileged scan examples, Metasploit handoff, intrusive NSE scripts, high-speed scanning, and firewall or IDS evasion guidance in SKILL.md. Most findings in templates and examples are false positives because they are documentation, public references, or educational snippets. No evidence found of prompt injection in the reviewed files.

remediation.suggestion: Remove decoy, source spoofing, idle scan, source-port bypass, packet fragmentation, and delayed split-scan instructions from marketplace-facing content.
Remove exploit, brute-force, denial-of-service, fuzzer, and intrusive script examples, or restrict them to a clearly separated controlled-lab reference.
Remove Metasploit handoff guidance from the published skill unless the marketplace explicitly accepts offensive exploitation workflows.

remediation.issue: Remote installer executed with curl pipe to shell
remediation.suggestion: Replace the pipe-to-shell installer with a pinned release, checksum verification, or a maintained GitHub Action.
Minimize sudo examples and explain safer alternatives, least-privilege requirements, and approved environments for raw-packet scans.
Add explicit refusal and scope-confirmation prompts before producing target-specific scan plans or commands.

content.value_statement: Network teams need repeatable guidance for authorized discovery and service review. This skill organizes Nmap workflows, safety checks, and reporting steps for approved scopes.
actual_capabilities: Guides host discovery, port scanning, service enumeration, OS detection, and vulnerability checks with Nmap.
Provides command examples for timing, rate limits, output formats, and report conversion.
Includes workflow steps for authorization, scope checks, logging, and validation.
Maps scanning activity to MITRE ATT&CK, PTES, OWASP, PCI-DSS, and ISO 27001 context.
Contains CI/CD and security-tool integration examples for scan output handling.
Documents defensive detection considerations for Nmap activity.
limitations: Requires clear authorization and a defined scanning scope before use.
Can disrupt systems if intrusive scripts, high scan rates, or evasion options are used.
Does not verify that a target is owned or approved.
Some examples require root privileges and local Nmap or Masscan installation.

use_cases.title: Inventory Approved Networks
use_cases.description: Create a controlled discovery plan for known IP ranges during an approved assessment window.

use_cases.title: Prepare Assessment Evidence
use_cases.description: Collect scan planning notes, command records, and reporting fields for audit evidence.

use_cases.title: Validate Exposure Findings
use_cases.description: Structure service enumeration and vulnerability checks for systems listed in a signed scope.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Authorized Discovery
prompt_templates.prompt: I have written approval for [IP range] during [time window]. Create a low-impact Nmap discovery plan with authorization checks and logging fields.

prompt_templates.title: Build Enumeration Steps
prompt_templates.prompt: For these approved hosts and ports, outline safe service enumeration steps, expected evidence, and validation notes.

prompt_templates.title: Review Scan Results
prompt_templates.prompt: Summarize these Nmap findings into confirmed services, likely false positives, business impact, and follow-up validation tasks.

prompt_templates.title: Design Controlled CI Scan
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a bounded CI network scan workflow for [environment] that includes approval gates, rate limits, artifact handling, and failure criteria.

output_examples.input: Plan discovery for an approved internal subnet during a two-hour window.
output_examples.output: The response defines scope checks, a staged discovery approach, rate controls, operator notes, and evidence fields for reporting.

output_examples.input: Review Nmap results that show exposed SSH, HTTPS, and database services.
output_examples.output: The response groups services by host, flags validation tasks, notes possible business impact, and recommends owner review.

output_examples.input: Create a reporting checklist for a vulnerability scan.
output_examples.output: The response lists authorization proof, command history, scan timing, affected hosts, findings, validation status, and remediation owners.

best_practices: Confirm written authorization, target ranges, scan windows, and emergency contacts before any scan.
Start with low-impact discovery and increase intensity only when scope permits it.
Record source address, timing, commands, targets, and validation notes for every run.
anti_patterns: Scanning public or third-party networks without explicit written approval.
Using evasion, brute-force, exploit, or denial-of-service scripts outside a signed scope.
Sharing scan outputs that expose hostnames, banners, vulnerabilities, or internal addresses.

faq.question: Is this skill only for authorized testing?
faq.answer: Yes. It should be used only for networks and systems covered by written approval.

faq.question: Does it run scans automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and examples. Users still choose tools, targets, and execution settings.

faq.question: Can scans disrupt services?
faq.answer: Yes. Aggressive timing, intrusive scripts, and high rates can affect systems and monitoring tools.

faq.question: What tools are expected?
faq.answer: The source references Nmap, Python, and Masscan. Some commands also require elevated privileges.

faq.question: Can it help with compliance evidence?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes logging, reporting, and mapping guidance for common security frameworks.

faq.question: Does it confirm vulnerabilities?
faq.answer: No. It helps organize detection and triage. Findings need manual validation before reporting.
